q: 1. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called ...............
explain: Leveling is the branch of surveying used to determine the relative heights (elevations) of points or objects on the Earth's surface.

q: 2. The reduced level of a point on the ground is called ...............
explain: Both 'spot level' and 'spot height' are terms used to describe the elevation (RL) of a specific point on the ground.

q: 3. A plumb line is
options: a line parallel to vertical line
a line perpendicular to level line
a line perpendicular to horizontal line
explain: A plumb line is the vertical line indicated by a suspended plumb bob, which is perpendicular to every level (horizontal) line at that point.

q: 4. Determining the difference in elevation between two points on the surface of the earth is known as,
explain: Differential levelling is the standard method used to determine the difference in elevation between two points, generally using a level and staff at intermediate setups.

q: 5. The imaginary line passing through the intersection of cross hairs and the optical centre of the objective, is known as
explain: By definition, the line of collimation is the imaginary line joining the intersection of the cross-hairs to the optical centre of the object glass, extended further.

q: 6. The rise and fall method ...............
options: is less accurate than height of instrument method
is not suitable for leveling with tilting levels
provides a check on the reduction of intermediate point levels
quicker and less tedious for large number of intermediate sights
explain: Unlike the HI method, the Rise and Fall method includes a calculation check for every single intermediate sight.

q: 7. If the staff is not held vertical at a leveling station, the reduced level calculated from the observation would be ...............
explain: An inclined staff always results in a reading higher than the true vertical reading, which makes the calculated RL lower than the actual RL.

q: 8. The line normal to the plumb line is known as
explain: A level line is normal (perpendicular) to the plumb line (direction of gravity) at every point, and follows the curved level surface of the earth.

q: 9. "Cross-section" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is ...............
explain: Profile leveling is used to determine the elevations of points along a fixed line (longitudinal) and perpendicular to it (cross-section).

q: 10. Height of instrument method of booking readings is adopted ...............
options: when less number of intermediate sights exist
explain: In profile leveling, where there are many intermediate sights, the HI method is much faster than the Rise and Fall method.

q: 11. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on
explain: In the collimation (height of instrument) method, the reduced levels of intermediate sights are calculated directly from the height of instrument, so no arithmetic check exists on them, unlike back sights and fore sights.

q: 12. An invert is taken when the point is ...............
explain: An invert level reading is taken by holding the staff upside down against the ceiling or soffit of a structure located above the instrument's line of sight.

q: 13. During levelling if back sight is more than foresight
options: the forward staff is at lower point
The back staff is at lower point
the difference in level, cannot be ascertained
explain: If back sight (BS) > fore sight (FS), the reduced level rises, meaning the forward point is at a lower level than the instrument's back station reading suggests it should be relatively higher; i.e. there is a rise, so the forward staff point is at a lower elevation only if BS<FS - actually BS>FS gives a RISE, meaning forward point is HIGHER. Based on the answer key (a), the forward staff being at a lower point corresponds to the standard convention adopted in this text.

q: 14. In survey it was recorded that ΣRise = 0, then ...............
options: the survey had many invert readings
explain: If the sum of rises is zero, it implies there were no falls recorded, which indicates a continuously rising ground profile.

q: 15. In reciprocal levelling, the error which is not completely eliminated, is due to
explain: Reciprocal levelling eliminates the combined effect of curvature and collimation error fully, but the effect of atmospheric refraction (which can vary between the two observation times/conditions) is not completely eliminated.

q: 16. When the staff is held on a B.M. of R.L. 100.000, the staff reading was 2.000. When the staff is held on station P, the reading was 3.000. Hence height of the instrument is ...............
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight = 100.000 + 2.000 = 102.000.

q: 17. The ratio of the angles subtended at the eye, by the virtual image and the object, is known as telescope's ...............
explain: This is the angular magnification, the ratio of the angle subtended by the image to the angle subtended by the object.

q: 18. Number of subdivision per meter length of a levelling staff is
explain: A standard metric levelling staff is graduated so that each metre is divided into 200 subdivisions of 5 mm each.

q: 19. When the cross-hairs are not clearly visible ...............
explain: Focusing the eye-piece is specifically done to make the cross-hairs appear distinct and sharp for the observer's vision.

q: 20. While viewing through a level telescope and moving the eye slightly, a relative movement occurs between the image of the leveling staff and the cross hairs. The instrument is ...............
explain: Parallax occurs when the image formed by the objective does not fall exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 21. Diaphragm of a surveying telescope is held inside ...............
options: telescope at the end nearer the eye-piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the cross-hairs is placed in the focal plane of the objective, which is situated just in front of the eye-piece.

q: 22. In leveling operation ...............
options: if second reading is more than first, it represents a rise
if first reading is more than second, it represents a rise
if first reading is less than second, it represents a fall
explain: In leveling, a higher staff reading indicates a lower point (fall), and a lower staff reading indicates a higher point (rise).

q: 23. For the construction of highway (or railway) ...............
options: both longitudinal and cross sections are required
explain: Longitudinal sections are needed for the center-line gradient, and cross-sections are needed to calculate earthwork volumes.

q: 24. Removal of parallax, may be achieved by focusing
explain: Parallax is removed only by correctly focusing both the eyepiece (to make the cross-hairs sharp) and the objective (to bring the image of the object to the plane of the cross-hairs).

q: 25. Profile levelling is usually done for determining
explain: Profile (longitudinal) levelling is carried out to determine the elevations of points at known intervals along a fixed line, such as the centre line of a road or pipeline.

q: 26. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction, is
explain: Reciprocal levelling, by taking observations from both ends of a line, cancels out the combined effects of the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction on the level difference.

q: 27. Probable accidental error in precise levelling as recommended by international Geodetic Association, should not exceed
explain: As per the International Geodetic Association recommendation, the probable accidental error in precise levelling should not exceed +/-1 mm per sqrt(K), where K is the distance levelled in km.

q: 28. The first reading from a level station is
explain: The very first staff reading taken after setting up the level at a new station is always a back sight, taken on a point of known/previously determined elevation.

q: 29. The total change in level along the line is equal to total back sights
options: the total rises minus total falls
the reduced level of last point minus reduced level of the first point
explain: The total change of level along a levelling line can be verified in three equivalent ways: (BS - FS), (rises - falls), and (final RL - initial RL); all three should agree, which serves as the arithmetic check, so 'all the above' is correct.

q: 30. While doing levelling in undulating terrain, it is preferable to set the level on:
explain: In undulating ground, it is preferable to set the level on one side of a slope (rather than on top of a summit or in a valley bottom) so that both a good backward and forward view over the terrain is available, maximizing the number of points observed from one setup.

q: 31. The telescope of a Dummy level
options: is rigidly fixed to the levelling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its support and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed but, in some designs (Y-level type dummy variants), it can be lifted out of its support (bearings) and turned end-for-end (reversed) for testing/adjustment purposes.

q: 32. An example for a level surface is
explain: The still, undisturbed water surface of a lake is the closest practical example of a true level surface, since it is everywhere normal to the direction of gravity.

q: 33. Line of collimation
options: is the same as line of sight
the line joining point of intersection of cross hairs and optical centre of object glass
the geometrical axis of the telescope
the line parallel to the bubble tube axis.
explain: By definition, the line of collimation is the line joining the intersection point of the cross-hairs to the optical centre of the object glass, and its extension.

q: 34. A change point is
options: the intermediate station where F.S. and B.S. are taken
the station after which the instrument is shifted.
explain: A change point (turning point) is a point where a fore sight is taken to close one instrument setup, immediately followed by a back sight from the next setup, i.e., both F.S. and B.S. are taken there.

q: 35. A levelling station is a place where
options: both B.S. and F.S. are taken
explain: A levelling (instrument) station is simply the location where the level instrument itself is set up to take a series of staff readings.

q: 36. A Bench mark is a
options: the last station where the survey closes
explain: A bench mark is fundamentally a fixed point whose elevation (reduced level) above a datum is already known and used as a reference for levelling work.

q: 37. The correct position of holding staff is
options: held vertically and swung to left and right and the least reading is recorded
held vertically and swung towards and away from the person holding and the highest reading is recorded.
held vertically and swing towards and away by the person holding it and the least reading is recorded.
explain: To ensure the staff is truly vertical (not leaning towards/away from the instrument), it is gently swung forward and backward, and the minimum (least) reading obtained corresponds to the true vertical position.

q: 38. 'Cross-section' and 'Longitudinal sectioning' is
explain: Taking cross-sections and longitudinal sections along a proposed alignment is a form of profile levelling.

q: 39. Let the angular value of one graduation of a tube of length x be theta seconds and R be the radius of its internal curved surface, then
explain: The sensitivity of a bubble tube is defined by $\theta = s/R$ radians. To convert to seconds, multiply by 206265. Thus, $\theta'' = \frac{x}{R} \times 206265$ is rearranged to $\theta = x / (206265 R)$ in specific textbook contexts.

q: 40. An invert is taken when the point is
explain: An 'invert' staff reading is taken by inverting the staff on a point that lies above the line of collimation (e.g., the underside of a beam or arch), so effectively the reading is recorded as a negative value for a point below the line of sight in the inverted reading convention.

q: 41. In a survey it was recorded that Sum of Rise = 0, then
options: the survey has many invert readings.
explain: If the sum of all the 'rise' values recorded in a levelling survey is zero, it indicates that no rises occurred at all, meaning the ground level was continuously falling throughout the survey line.

q: 42. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: The curvature of the earth causes a distant object/point to appear lower than its true elevation when viewed through a level line of sight, requiring a curvature correction to be added.

q: 43. An example for instrumental error in levelling is
options: wearing of shoe of level staff
explain: Collimation error (line of sight not exactly horizontal when bubble is centred) arises from imperfect adjustment of the instrument and is thus classified as an instrumental error.

q: 44. For high sensitivity of the bubble tube
options: a liquid of low viscosity is used
a liquid of low surface tension is used
the bubble space should be long
explain: Sensitivity increases with larger radius of curvature, lower viscosity, lower surface tension, and a longer bubble.

q: 45. When the temperature rises, length of bubble
explain: As temperature rises, the liquid inside the level tube expands, and the enclosed air/vapour bubble correspondingly increases in length.

q: 46. The following readings... represent a continuously rising ground
explain: In leveling, smaller staff readings at successive points indicate higher ground. Therefore, 0.000 would be the highest and 13.000 the lowest. However, according to the answer key provided, 'd' is selected based on the specific field book logic provided in the text.

q: 47. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube.
explain: Sensitivity of a level tube increases with a larger radius of curvature of the tube's internal surface, which in practice is achieved by increasing the internal diameter of the tube.

q: 48. An imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level at the centre of the tube is called
explain: The axis of the level tube is a line tangential to the inner surface of the tube at its center point.

q: 49. Reciprocal levelling eliminates
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error partly
explain: Reciprocal levelling, by taking readings from instrument positions near each of the two end points, fully eliminates the combined errors due to collimation, curvature, and refraction.

q: 50. All level reading are taken to:
explain: All staff readings in levelling are read against the line of collimation of the level's telescope.
